nodes.content: Develop textual entailment models that generalize to unseen quantifier scope compositions while distinguishing semantic changes from paraphrases.
requirements: Achieve at least 85% balanced accuracy on entailment, contradiction, and neutrality across unseen scope compositions.
Preserve predictions across 95% of meaning-preserving paraphrases while detecting 90% of label-changing scope reversals.

nodes.content: Train ScopeGraph-NLI with compositional scope-graph supervision, paraphrase-consistency loss, and label-aware contrastive training on scope reversals.
Can ScopeGraph-NLI handle held-out three-quantifier scope permutations while preserving passive paraphrases and detecting label-changing reversals?
ScopeGraph-NLI will reach 85% three-class balanced accuracy on held-out three-quantifier permutations, 95% passive-paraphrase agreement, and 90% scope-reversal detection.
Construct ScopeSplit-3 with held-out scope permutations, train ScopeGraph-NLI, then measure balanced accuracy, passive-paraphrase agreement, and scope-reversal detection.
Train ScopeGraph-NLI on 24,000 ScopeSplit-3 examples; score 3,000 held-out permutations, 1,000 passive paraphrases, and 1,000 label-changing reversals.
ScopeGraph-NLI achieved 86.7% balanced accuracy on held-out permutations, 96.1% passive-paraphrase agreement, and 91.4% label-changing scope-reversal detection.
Advance ScopeGraph-NLI to broader quantifier benchmarks because ScopeSplit-3 exceeds all three prespecified thresholds.
ScopeSplit-3 v1 bundle contains the ScopeGraph-NLI checkpoint, 5,000 evaluation pairs, and scripts for all three metrics.
Using ScopeSplit-3 v1, retrain ablations without scope supervision, paraphrase consistency, or reversal contrastive training; compare all three metrics.
Across five ScopeSplit-3 seeds, ScopeGraph-NLI averaged 82.6% balanced accuracy versus 85.1% without scope supervision.
Without scope supervision, ScopeGraph-NLI will average ≥85% balanced accuracy, ≥95% paraphrase agreement, and ≥90% reversal detection across five seeds.
Audit five seed-matched no-scope-supervision ScopeGraph-NLI checkpoints on ScopeSplit-3 v1, measuring balanced accuracy, paraphrase agreement, and reversal detection.
Five no-scope-supervision seeds averaged 85.1% balanced accuracy, 95.5% passive-paraphrase agreement, and 90.6% label-changing reversal detection on ScopeSplit-3.
Train DenotationNLI on finite-model truth tables with paraphrase orbits and counterfactual scope swaps, without scope-graph supervision.
Generate finite-model truth tables, train DenotationNLI with paraphrase orbits and scope swaps, then assess ScopeSplit-3 metrics across five seeds.
Using ScopeSplit-3 v1 scripts, generate 40,000 finite-model truth-table pairs and train five DenotationNLI seeds with paraphrase and swap objectives.
DenotationNLI v0.1 bundle contains 40,000 finite-model training pairs, five checkpoints, and ScopeSplit-3-compatible evaluation scripts.
Run five-seed ScopeSplit-3 v1 evaluation of DenotationNLI v0.1 and ScopeGraph-NLI, comparing balanced accuracy, paraphrase agreement, and reversal detection.
Across five ScopeSplit-3 seeds, DenotationNLI achieved 87.0% balanced accuracy, 96.0% paraphrase agreement, and 92.0% reversal detection; ScopeGraph-NLI averaged 82.6% accuracy.
Does DenotationNLI retain its ScopeSplit-3 gains on unseen quantifier lexemes and larger finite domains, rather than memorizing truth tables?
On LexDomain-8’s unseen quantifiers and eight-object domains, DenotationNLI will retain ≥85% balanced accuracy, ≥95% paraphrase agreement, and ≥90% reversal detection.
Evaluate five DenotationNLI v0.1 checkpoints on LexDomain-8’s unseen lexemes and eight-object domains for balanced accuracy, paraphrase agreement, and reversal detection.
On LexDomain-8, five DenotationNLI seeds averaged 85.8% balanced accuracy, 95.4% paraphrase agreement, and 90.8% reversal detection.
Run leakage-controlled LexDomain-8 tests on DenotationNLI v0.1 with unseen lexemes and disjoint eight-object graphs; score balanced accuracy, paraphrase agreement, reversals.
On graph-disjoint LexDomain-8, five DenotationNLI seeds averaged 79.2% balanced accuracy, 94.1% paraphrase agreement, and 84.5% reversal detection.
Structure-diverse finite-model training will restore DenotationNLI to ≥85% balanced accuracy, ≥95% paraphrase agreement, and ≥90% reversal detection on graph-disjoint LexDomain-8.
Extend DenotationNLI v0.1 with graph-diverse truth tables; retrain five seeds and score graph-disjoint LexDomain-8 accuracy, paraphrase agreement, reversals.
On graph-disjoint LexDomain-8, five structure-diverse DenotationNLI seeds averaged 85.9% balanced accuracy, 95.2% paraphrase agreement, and 90.3% reversal detection.
Build ScopeProof-NLI with paraphrase-canonicalized scope forests and first-order countermodel search to distinguish genuine reversals across unseen compositions.
Can ScopeProof-NLI preserve passive-voice equivalence without conflating distinct readings of ambiguous three-quantifier sentences?
On AmbiScope-3, ScopeProof-NLI will achieve ≥95% passive-equivalence agreement and ≥90% detection of label-changing three-quantifier readings.
Annotate AmbiScope-3 scope forests, canonicalize active/passive pairs, train ScopeProof-NLI, and measure equivalence agreement and reading-change detection.
Using DenotationNLI v0.1 assets, train ScopeProof-NLI; evaluate AmbiScope-3 passive/reversal metrics and structure-diverse DenotationNLI on graph-disjoint LexDomain-8.

ScopeProof-NLI: 96.2% passive agreement, 91.3% label-changing reversal detection on AmbiScope-3; structure-diverse DenotationNLI: 86.0% accuracy, 95.3% agreement, 90.5% reversals, graph-disjoint LexDomain-8.
AmbiScope-3 v1 provides annotated three-quantifier scope forests, active/passive pairs, label-changing reversals, and ScopeProof-NLI evaluation code.
Using AmbiScope-3 v1, ablate ScopeProof-NLI’s scope-forest canonicalization and countermodel search; measure held-out accuracy, passive agreement, and reversal detection.
On AmbiScope-3, removing both components lowered balanced accuracy 86.4%→80.7%, passive agreement 96.2%→91.0%, and reversal detection 91.3%→82.4%.
Retrain ScopeProof-NLI across six leave-one-permutation-out AmbiScope-3 v1 splits; score balanced accuracy, passive agreement, and reversal detection.
Across six held-out AmbiScope-3 permutations, ScopeProof-NLI averaged 79.8% balanced accuracy, 93.2% passive agreement, and 84.6% reversal detection.
Do scope-forest parsing errors or countermodel-search failures explain ScopeProof-NLI’s 79.8% balanced accuracy on held-out permutations?
Oracle scope forests will restore held-out AmbiScope-3 to ≥85% balanced accuracy, ≥95% passive agreement, and ≥90% reversal detection, implicating parsing.
On AmbiScope-3 v1, compare oracle versus predicted scope forests across held-out permutations; measure balanced accuracy, passive agreement, reversals, countermodel failures.
Oracle forests raised held-out AmbiScope-3 accuracy 79.8%→87.2%, passive agreement 93.2%→96.0%, and reversal detection 84.6%→91.1%.
Retain canonicalization and countermodel search, but prioritize scope-forest parser repair before deployment: oracle forests recover held-out thresholds.
Train LatticeScope-NLI with countermodel-guided scope-forest parsing, paraphrase-aligned lattices, and reversal-contrastive decoding to address held-out parsing errors.
Distill AmbiScope-3 oracle forests into LatticeScope-NLI, align passive paraphrases, contrast reversals, then evaluate six held-out permutations.
Train LatticeScope-NLI on DenotationNLI v0.1’s 40,000 pairs using oracle-forest distillation motivated by 7.4-point accuracy recovery and paraphrase/reversal losses.
LatticeScope-NLI v0.1 contains oracle-distilled scope-forest parser checkpoints, paraphrase-alignment and reversal-contrastive training code, and six-split evaluation scripts.
Evaluate LatticeScope-NLI v0.1 on six leave-one-permutation-out AmbiScope-3 splits for balanced accuracy, passive agreement, and label-changing reversal detection.
Across six held-out AmbiScope-3 permutations, LatticeScope-NLI averaged 86.1% balanced accuracy, 95.6% passive agreement, and 90.7% reversal detection.
Using LatticeScope-NLI v0.1, ablate oracle-forest distillation, paraphrase alignment, and reversal contrast individually across six held-out AmbiScope-3 permutations.
Without reversal-contrastive decoding, six-split accuracy rose 86.1%→87.4%, reversal detection 90.7%→93.1%, and passive agreement stayed 95.6%.
Are ambiguous-scope hard negatives mislabeled, causing reversal-contrastive decoding’s 2.4-point reversal-detection deficit on held-out permutations?
At least 10% of AmbiScope-3 ambiguous reversal negatives are mislabeled; correcting them raises contrastive reversal detection above 93.1%.
Adjudicate 300 AmbiScope-3 ambiguous reversal negatives; correct labels, retrain LatticeScope-NLI v0.1, and measure six-split reversal detection.
Only 2.0% of 300 negatives needed relabeling; corrected contrastive training reached 91.0% six-split reversal detection, below 93.1% without contrast.
Overlapping scope forests, not mislabeled negatives, cause contrastive collisions; masking overlaps will exceed 93.1% six-split reversal detection.
Mask negatives sharing an oracle scope reading in LatticeScope-NLI v0.1; retrain six AmbiScope-3 splits against 93.1% reversal-detection baseline.
Masking overlapping scope-forest negatives raised six-split reversal detection from 90.7% to 94.0%, exceeding the 93.1% no-contrast baseline.
Adopt overlap-masked reversal contrast: detection rises from 90.7% to 94.0%, outperforming contrast removal (93.1%) and relabeling (91.0%).
